page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a massive 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core.

This instance includes 2835 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, allowing for high-throughput disk configurations. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for accelerated mathematical and machine learning operations, alongside hardware-assisted cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA_NI).

In benchmark evaluations, the D48ds_v7 demonstrates strong performance profiles. It achieves a Passmark CPU score of 68,963.55 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 275.64 GB/sec. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, with uncached read bandwidth reaching 259.05 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 106.22 GB/sec. The system also shows high throughput in database operations, processing 84.18 million Redis SET operations per second. This high resource density and strong memory bandwidth provide favorable qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial compute and memory throughput without the premium cost of memory-optimized tiers.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio, large local storage, and strong database and compression benchmarks, the D48ds_v7 is well suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and medium-scale data processing tasks. It is also capable of handling CPU-based machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its prompt processing speed of 239.1 tokens/second on a 7B parameter model.
